reasoning: The document has multiple major structural issues that prevent auto-approval. Both the LLM and programmatic signals identified that nested lists were flattened and running headers/images were erroneously extracted into the body content on nearly every page. Additionally, the heading hierarchy is broken for sibling sections. With an LLM composite score of 0.7133 and clear structural defects, this requires human intervention.

concerns.analysis: Checked heading levels for consistency and proper nesting. In the source PDF, all 'PE-*' sections (e.g., PE-6, PE-7, PE-8, PE-10) are formatted at the exact same visual level (same font size, bold weight). However, the output assigns inconsistent heading levels to these siblings. For instance, 'PE-6 (1)', 'PE-10', and 'PE-11' are rendered as H2, while 'PE-7', 'PE-8', 'PE-9', 'PE-14', 'PE-16', and 'PE-17' are nested incorrectly as H3.

Examined list nesting structures. The source document features nested lists with alphabetical parent items (a, b, c) and roman numeral sub-items (i, ii, iii). On pages where list continuation spans a page break, the output flattens the hierarchy. For example, on page 3, the sub-items 'i' through 'viii' are rendered as top-level siblings to parent items 'e' and 'f'. A similar flattening occurs on page 12.
